citeAs: Wadhawan, R., Bansal, H., Chang, K.-W., and Peng, N. (2024). CONTEXTUAL: Evaluating Context-Sensitive Text-Rich Visual Reasoning in Large Multimodal Models. Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235.
creator: Rohan Wadhawan, Hritik Bansal, Kai-Wei Chang, Nanyun Peng (University of California Los Angeles)
description: CONTEXTUAL is a context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning dataset consisting of 506 challenging human-crafted instructions for evaluating large multimodal models. It covers eight real-world visual scenarios (time reading, shopping, navigation, abstract scenes, mobile application, webpages, infographics, and miscellaneous natural scenes), where each instance contains a human-written instruction and a human-written ground-truth response requiring joint reasoning over embedded text and visual context in images.
name: CONTEXTUAL
rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 (for human evaluation: each model response was shown to three human annotators independently)
rai:annotatorDemographics: Human annotators were mainly from the US (for human performance baseline and human evaluation). MTurk workers who passed a qualification test were used for human performance baseline. Authors (researchers at UCLA) performed the primary annotation of instruction-response pairs.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: MTurk workers verified 96% of samples were annotated correctly. For human evaluation, majority vote among three annotators was used as the final decision. Correlation between human and automatic evaluation metrics was measured using ROC-AUC and Spearman correlation; GPT-4 evaluation achieved the highest ROC-AUC of 85.9 and Spearman correlation of 0.71.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk) for verification of annotations, human performance baseline, and human evaluation of model responses
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Stage 1: Images were shortlisted via manual filtering (for Time, Shopping, Navigation, Abstract) or heuristic-based filtering using PaddleOCR (selecting top 500 images with highest word count). Stage 2: Authors divided into two groups each annotating four categories, strictly following annotation guidelines. Stage 3: MTurk workers (mutually exclusive from human baseline and evaluation workers) verified correctness of each sample; 96% were annotated correctly. Incorrect samples were filtered, and each author group reviewed the other group's samples to ensure guideline adherence and filter low-quality samples.
rai:dataBiases: Human annotators were mainly from the US, which may introduce linguistic and cultural bias in the human baseline responses and evaluations. The dataset avoids instructions solvable by text-based reasoning alone (OCR+LLM), specifically designed to require visual context. GPT-4V may have been tuned on memes and quotes data, leading it to outperform humans on abstract contexts.
rai:dataCollection: Images were sourced from six different sources: LAION-5B (for Time, Shopping, Navigation, Abstract categories via CLIP-retrieval UI keyword search), Rico Dataset (for Application Usage), Open WebText Initiative website screenshots (for Web Usage), and test sets of existing VQA datasets (InfographicVQA for Infographic; STVQA and ESTVQA for Miscellaneous Natural Scenes). Authors were divided into two groups to annotate instruction-response pairs, with MTurk workers verifying correctness.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images from LAION-5B (retrieved via CLIP-retrieval UI keyword search), Rico Dataset (66,000 distinct UI screens from 9,300 Android apps), website screenshots from Open WebText Initiative links, and images from test sets of InfographicVQA, STVQA, and ESTVQA datasets.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: Human annotators were mainly from the US, limiting linguistic diversity and writing style variation. The dataset focuses on English-language text in images. Model responses may hallucinate, though no apparent harmful or privacy-sensitive information was observed. The extension of the work could focus on understanding the impact of different social groups on human baseline performance.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract categories: manual filtering of images for suitability. For Application Usage, Web Usage, Infographic, and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes: heuristic-based filtering using PaddleOCR to detect text, selecting the top 500 images with the highest number of words.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: A subset of 100 samples (validation set) is released with reference responses; the remaining 406 samples are kept hidden. A continuously updated leaderboard is maintained on HuggingFace.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to advance LMM capabilities for real-world applications such as assisting the visually impaired in navigating text-rich scenes. The authors ensured images, instructions, and responses are not offensive to any social group. They acknowledge that human annotators were mainly from the US, which may limit linguistic diversity, and suggest future work should involve annotators from more diverse regions.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning capabilities of large multimodal models; benchmarking LMMs on joint reasoning over embedded text and visual context in images; assessing performance across diverse real-world visual scenarios including navigation, shopping, time reading, and infographics.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: PaddleOCR (PP-OCRv4 model) used for text detection during image filtering; CLIP-retrieval UI used for keyword-based image retrieval from LAION-5B

evidence.rai:dataCollection: CONTEXTUAL comprises images sourced from six different sources. Firstly, we obtain images for the Time ,Shopping ,Navigation &Abstract categories from the LAION-5B (Schuhmann et al., 2022). Specifically, we use keyword search using CLIP-retrieval UI (Beaumont, 2022). ... Secondly, we source images for the Application Usage category from the Rico Dataset (Deka et al., 2017) ... Thirdly, we scrape the website links made available by the Open WebText Initiative (Gokaslan & Cohen, 2019) and collect screenshots for the Web Usage category.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionRawData: we source images for the Application Usage category from the Rico Dataset (Deka et al., 2017), which includes 66,000 distinct UI screens originating from 9,300 Android apps. Thirdly, we scrape the website links made available by the Open WebText Initiative (Gokaslan & Cohen, 2019) and collect screenshots for the Web Usage category. Lastly, we acquire images from the test sets of existing VQA datasets

evidence.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Stage 2: We divide the authors into two groups, namely Group 1 and Group 2, each responsible for annotating four specific categories. The authors strictly adhered to the provided annotation guidelines throughout the annotation. Stage 3: In this final stage, we perform a verification process for each sample annotated in Stage 2. We asked MTurk workers (mutually exclusive from the ones used for human performance baseline and human evaluation) to verify the correctness of each sample < image, instruction, response > and found that 96% of the samples were annotated correctly.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: We also benchmark the performance of humans on our dataset using Amazon Mechanical Turk. The selected annotators that pass an qualification test were asked to write accurate responses for all the instruction-image from the dataset.
evidence.rai:annotationsPerItem: we show each model response, without revealing the model identity, to three human annotators independently. Specifically, the human annotators are asked to decide the predicted response is acceptable given the reference response, instruction and image from the dataset.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: We asked MTurk workers ... to verify the correctness of each sample < image, instruction, response > and found that 96% of the samples were annotated correctly. ... we report the acceptance rating (0-100 in percentage) of the responses using the majority vote among the three annotator as the final decision.
evidence.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The images that are categorized under Time ,Shopping ,Navigation , and Abstract undergo manual filtering to guarantee their suitability for annotation. However, for Application Usage ,Web Usage ,Infographic , andMiscellaneous Natural Scenes , we perform heuristic-based filtering. Specifically, we employ a PaddleOCR (paddlepadle, 2023) to detect the text in the image. Subsequently, we select the top 500 images with the highest number of words

evidence.rai:dataUseCases: we introduce CONTEXTUAL , a dataset for evaluating the text-rich visual reasoning in large multimodal models. Going beyond the prior efforts that focus primarily on the testing the reading skills in the visual contexts, we create novel and challenging instructions from scratch that would require the models to capture the context in which the text is presented in an image.
